title: "Heart Disease Deaths in Michigan, 2000-2023"
output:
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    orientation: columns
    vertical_layout: fill
    theme: cosmo
    source_code: embed
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(leaflet)
library(DT)
library(tigris)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# Read Michigan data
mi_wide <- read_csv("COUNTandPOP2000to2023.csv")

# Create Michigan county boundaries
mi_map <- counties(
  state = "MI",
  cb = TRUE,
  year = 2020,
  progress_bar = FALSE
) |>
  st_transform(4326)

# Reshape data into one row per county per year
mi_long <- mi_wide |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `2000`:`2023`,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "Y"
  ) |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))

# Get statewide death counts
mi_state <- mi_long |>
  filter(County == "Michigan") |>
  select(year, State_Deaths = Y)

# Get statewide midpoint population
state_population <- mi_wide |>
  filter(County == "Michigan") |>
  pull(Population)

# Remove statewide row and prepare county data
mi <- mi_long |>
  filter(County != "Michigan")

# Create county GEOID lookup
county_lookup <- mi_map |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  transmute(
    County = NAME,
    GEOID = as.character(GEOID)
  )

# Join GEOIDs to Michigan county data
mi <- mi |>
  left_join(county_lookup, by = "County")

# Calculate expected deaths and SIR
#mi <- mi |>
#  left_join(mi_state, by = "year") |>
#  mutate(
#    State_Rate = (State_Deaths / state_population) * 100000,
#    E = Population * State_Rate / 100000,
#    SIR = Y / E
#  )

# Calculate overall Michigan death rate (2000-2023)
State_Rate <- (sum(mi_state$State_Deaths) /
                 (state_population * nrow(mi_state))) * 100000

# Calculate expected deaths and SIR
mi <- mi |>
  mutate(
    E = Population * State_Rate / 100000,
    SIR = Y / E
  )

# For the map: one row per county
by_county <- mi |>
  group_by(GEOID) |>
  summarise(
    Y = sum(Y),
    E = sum(E),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(SIR = Y / E)

mi_map <- left_join(mi_map, by_county, by = "GEOID")

# For the time series: one row per year
focus <- "Wayne"

#by_year <- bind_rows(
#  mi |>
#    group_by(year) |>
#    summarise(Y = sum(Y), E = sum(E), .groups = "drop") |>
#    mutate(area = "Michigan"),
#  mi |>
#    filter(County == focus) |>
#    mutate(area = focus)
#) |>
#  mutate(SIR = Y / E)

# Calculate annual SIR for Michigan and Wayne County
by_year <- bind_rows(

  # Michigan statewide
  mi_state |>
    mutate(
      E = state_population * State_Rate / 100000,
      Y = State_Deaths,
      SIR = Y / E,
      area = "Michigan"
    ) |>
    select(year, Y, E, SIR, area),

  # Wayne County
  mi |>
    filter(County == focus) |>
    mutate(area = focus) |>
    select(year, Y, E, SIR, area)
)
```

Column {data-width=600}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Standardized incidence ratio (SIR) by county, 1968--1988

```{r map}

breaks <- c(0, 0.5, 2/3, 0.9, 1/0.9, 1.5, 2, Inf)

pal <- colorBin(rev(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(7, "RdBu")),
                domain = mi_map$SIR, bins = breaks)

# "CartoDB.Positron" doesnt work, so I subbed it with the help of AI
# colors are chosen because blue can symbolize better, red for struggling counties, and white for counties that are perfoming as expected

leaflet(mi_map) |>
  addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldTopoMap") |>
  addControl(
    html = "<h4>SIR by county, Heart disease deaths from 2000 to 2023</h4>",
    position = "topright"
  ) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal(SIR), fillOpacity = 0.8,
    color = "white", weight = 1,
    label = ~sprintf("%s: SIR %.2f (%.0f observed, %.0f expected)",
                     NAME, SIR, Y, E),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 2, color = "black",
                                        bringToFront = TRUE)
  ) |>
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = ~SIR, title = "SIR",
            labFormat = labelFormat(digits = 2), opacity = 0.8)
```

> SIR = observed / expected. Red: more cases than expected; blue: fewer.

Column {data-width=400}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### SIR by year (dashed line: as many cases as expected)

```{r timeseries}
cols <- setNames(c("black", "#B2182B"), c("Michigan", focus))

p <- ggplot(by_year, aes(year, SIR, colour = area)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "SIR", colour = NULL, title = "SIR for Michigan and Wayne County, using deaths from heart disease (2000 to 2023)") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(p)                                  # hover, zoom


```

Note: table shows that wayne county (Detroit, largest county) has historically had a much higher SIR than the state average. However, rates have dramatically fallen since, and Wayne has dropped below the state as of 2023. 


### Counties

```{r table}
mi_map |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  transmute(County = NAME, Observed = Y,
            Expected = round(E, 1), SIR = round(SIR, 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(SIR)) |>
  datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10))
```

> Data: Moraga (2019), Ch. 7. Boundaries: US Census Bureau, via `tigris`.

AI use note: used AI to use the dataset properly and to adapt it to the module, used help for errors
